Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

quote.after:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

(The contradiction package from a closure relation.) Let $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a future-inextendible future causal curve and $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ a past-inextendible future causal curve such that for all $t_+\ge0$, $t_-\le0$ there are $u_k\le v_k$ with $u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$. Then this situation is impossible. Indeed, by [L2] there is an inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^+$ extending $\alpha^+$ with $\gamma^+|_{[0,\infty)}=\alpha^+$ and an inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^-$ whose restriction to $(-\infty,0]$ is $\alpha^-$. By the crossing property, step 2.1, there are $t_+'\in[0,\infty)$ with $\alpha^+(t_+')\in I^+(S)$ (take $t_+'$ larger than the unique $S$-parameter of $\gamma^+$ and than $0$) and $t_-'\le0$ with $\alpha^-(t_-')\in I^-(S)$. Choose $s_1\in S$ with $s_1\ll\alpha^+(t_+')$ and $s_2\in S$ with $\alpha^-(t_-')\ll s_2$. Let $u_k\le v_k$ be the corresponding sequences. Since $I^+(s_1)$ is open and contains $\alpha^+(t_+')$, for large $k$ we have $s_1\ll u_k$; since $I^-(s_2)$ is open and contains $\alpha^-(t_-')$, for large $k$ we have $v_k\ll s_2$. Fix such a $k$. Then $s_1\ll u_k\le v_k$, so $s_1\ll v_k$ by [L4]; and $s_1\ll v_k\ll s_2$, so $s_1\ll s_2$ by transitivity of $\ll$ [L4]. If $s_1\ne s_2$, this contradicts the acausality of $S$ [L1]. If $s_1=s_2=:s$, then the concatenation of a future timelike curve from $s$ to $u_k$, the future causal curve from $u_k$ to $v_k$ and a future timelike curve from $v_k$ to $s$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $s$ (nonconstant because $s\ll u_k$), contradicting step 1.1.

(The causal relation is closed.) Let $p_k\le q_k$ with $p_k\to p$ and $q_k\to q$. If infinitely many $p_k=q_k$, then $p=q$ (by uniqueness of limits) and $p\le q$. Otherwise, for large $k$ choose a future causal curve $\gamma_k$ with $\gamma_k(0')=p_k$, $\gamma_k(1')=q_k$ and reparametrize it by $h$-arclength: $\beta_k:[0,L_k]\to M$, $\beta_k(0)=p_k$, $\beta_k(L_k)=q_k$; the $L_k$ are positive. If the sequence $L_k$ is bounded, clause (i) of [L3] (applied to a subsequence with $L_k\to b$) gives a future causal curve $\beta:[0,b]\to M$ from $p$ to $q$, and either $b>0$ and $p\le q$ via $\beta$, or $b=0$, in which case $p=q$ by clause (i) and $p\le p$. If $L_k\to\infty$ along a subsequence, clause (ii) of [L3] gives future-inextendible $\alpha^+$ from $p$ and past-inextendible $\alpha^-$ to $q$ with the closure relation, which is impossible by step 3.1. Hence $p\le q$.

(Strong causality.) Suppose strong causality fails at $p\in M$ with neighbourhood $U$. By [L5] there are an open $W\ni p$ with $\overline W\subseteq U$ and future causal curves $\sigma_k:[0,1]\to M$ with endpoints $x_k,y_k\in W$, $x_k\to p$, $y_k\to p$, and $\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq W$ for every $k$. Fix a coordinate ball $B=x^{-1}(B_{r_0})\subseteq W$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and let $c_1:=\sqrt c\,r_0>0$, where $c>0$ is a lower bound for the $h$-length density on the closed coordinate ball against the Euclidean coordinate speed ([[lem-local-comparison-of-a-riemannian-metric-with-the-euclidean-metric]], [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] clause (a)). Then every locally absolutely continuous curve $\eta$ joining $p$ to a point outside $B$ has $\ell_h(\eta)\ge c_1$: let $\tau$ be its first exit time from $B$, so that $x(\eta(\tau))$ lies on the sphere of radius $r_0$ and $$r_0\le|x(\eta(\tau))-x(\eta(0))|_{\mathrm e}\le\int_0^\tau|(x\circ\eta)'|_{\mathrm e}\le c^{-1/2}\ell_h(\eta|_{[0,\tau]})\le c^{-1/2}\ell_h(\eta).$$ Reparametrize each $\sigma_k$ by $h$-arclength: $\alpha_k:[0,L_k]\to M$, $\alpha_k(0)=x_k$, $\alpha_k(L_k)=y_k$. Choose $z_k\in\sigma_k([0,1])\setminus W\subseteq M\setminus B$ and let $\tau_k$ be the first parameter at which $\alpha_k$ exits $B$; for large $k$ we have $x_k\in B$, so $0<\tau_k\le L_k$ and the estimate applied to $\eta:=\alpha_k|_{[0,\tau_k]}$ gives $L_k\ge\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[0,\tau_k]})\ge c_1>0$ for all large $k$. If $L_k$ is bounded along a subsequence, clauses (i) and (iii) of [L3] (with $x=z=p$ and $b=\lim L_k\ge c_1>0$) produce a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $p$, contradicting step 1.1. If $L_k\to\infty$, clause (ii) of [L3] produces the impossible configuration of step 3.1. Hence strong causality holds at every $p$.

(The causal diamonds are compact.) Let $p,q\in M$ and $A:=J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$; it is closed in $M$ because $J^+(p)$ and $J^-(q)$ are closed by step 4.1 (with the first, respectively second, argument constant). With the metric $d_h$ inducing the manifold topology [L6], $A$ is a closed subset of the metric space $(M,d_h)$; if $A$ were not compact, then by [L7] it would not be sequentially compact, so there would be $r_k\in A$ with no subsequence converging in $A$, hence none converging in $M$ (limits of convergent sequences in a closed set lie in the set). For each $k$ choose a future causal curve from $p$ to $q$ through $r_k$, and reparametrize it by $h$-arclength: $\gamma_k:[0,M_k]\to M$ with $\gamma_k(0)=p$, $\gamma_k(M_k)=q$ and $\gamma_k(s_k)=r_k$. If the lengths $M_k$ were bounded along a subsequence, clause (i) of [L3] with $x=p=:z$ and $b:=\lim M_k$ would give a limit curve through $p$ and $q$, and $r_k=\gamma_k(s_k)$ would converge to $\gamma(s_*)$ for an accumulation point $s_*$ of the bounded sequence $s_k$: contradiction. Hence $M_k\to\infty$, and clause (ii) of [L3] produces the impossible configuration of step 3.1: contradiction. Therefore $A$ is compact.

(Conclusion.) Clause (a) is step 1.1, clause (b) is step 4.2, and clause (c) is step 5.1; strong causality and compactness of all causal diamonds are exactly the definition of global hyperbolicity in [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c).
